features.title: Keep your head in the problem.
features.description: A place for the statement, your working solution, and the cases that help you get it right.

items.title: One round. Room for every problem.
items.body: Move between statements in one contest tab. Separate folders keep your work organized, whether you start with A or skip straight to C.

items.title: Start with your own setup.
items.body: Choose your language and starter template. Each language keeps its own source file, with your usual completion, extensions, and shortcuts.

items.title: Find the mismatch.
items.body: Run samples and add your own cases. Inspect stdout, stderr, and the first differing token instead of guessing where the output went wrong.

items.title: Add the round before the countdown.
items.body: Leave VS Code running and released statements and samples download automatically, with retries if a download fails.

items.title: Read it another way.
items.body: Connect your AI provider and translate into one of nine languages. Translate as needed or after import, and switch back to the original statement anytime.

items.title: Check it. Confirm it. Send it.
items.body: Optional Codeforces login unlocks experimental submission with an explicit confirmation and verdict notifications. Copying to the official submit page is also available.

items.title: Know where you stand.
items.body: Check public submissions and standings, find your handle, then return to the next problem without opening another contest tab.

items.title: Keep the useful replies.
items.body: A local input/output cache reuses identical AI requests. Choose its limits or turn it off; API keys live separately in secure storage.

steps.title: Bring a problem—or the whole round.
steps.body: Import a Codeforces contest, pick a single problem, or create a local exercise. Each collection keeps its own list, newest first.

steps.title: Work the way you already do.
steps.body: Read the statement beside your native VS Code editor. New solutions use your chosen language and template; optional AI translation is there when you need it.

steps.title: Put your solution to the test.
steps.body: Run samples, try edge cases, and inspect the output. When you are ready, confirm a one-click submission or copy your code to Codeforces.

workflow.notice: Codeforces login and direct submission are experimental. Site verification may block them; local practice and copy-and-open submission remain available.

principles.description: Your shortcuts, language extensions, and compiler stay yours. Codeforces Workbench adds the round and its problems to the workspace you already use.
principles.localBody: No Codeforces Workbench account is needed to write and test solutions locally.
principles.honestBody: Codeforces site verification can interrupt downloads, login, or submission. Keep the official website handy as a fallback.

items.a: Codeforces Workbench is an extension for desktop VS Code. Install it in your existing editor to work on Codeforces problems.

items.q: Do I need to install a compiler or runtime?
items.a: Install the compiler or runtime required by your chosen language. Codeforces tools are already bundled in the platform-specific VSIX, so there is no separate CF Tool or downloader to install.

items.q: Can it submit directly to Codeforces?
items.a: Yes, experimentally: log in under Environment checks, select the official compiler and confirm the upload. Exact submissions are monitored for verdict notifications. Site verification may block login or submission; copy-and-open remains available.
Saved code, custom tests, and cached statements remain available. Downloads, rankings, and public submissions require a network connection.

steps: Download the matching 0.1.0 Alpha VSIX below, or install Codeforces Workbench by AC-Stride from the Marketplace. Choose the pre-release version if offered.

download.warning: Local programs run on your computer, not in a security sandbox. Use only code you trust.

docs.title: Your first run.
docs.intro: Install the extension, check your tools, and run your first set of samples.

sections.title: 01 / Set up your environment
sections.body: Install a matching VSIX and open a trusted local folder. In Codeforces Workbench Settings → Environment checks, configure the tools for your preferred language and run the checks. Login is optional for local work.

sections.title: 02 / Import a contest or problem
sections.body: The sidebar has Contests, Codeforces Problems and Local Practice. Each plus imports or creates an item using your default language. Downloads and bounded retries are automatic; selecting a missing statement starts recovery. Adding a contest does not register you.

sections.title: 03 / Read and write
sections.body: Contests use one editor tab named after the round. Its left rail switches between overview/rankings and problem statements; the header shows ended/countdown status. Standalone problems omit the multi-problem rail. Source files for different languages stay separate.

sections.title: 04 / Run your cases
sections.body: Use sample tabs or add a custom case with +. Run all saves the selected solution before testing. Compare expected and actual output; local AC is not an official verdict.

sections.title: 05 / Submit with confirmation
sections.body: Log in to Codeforces under Environment checks. One-click submit saves the current code, asks for an official compiler and requires confirmation; verdicts appear as VS Code notifications. Without login, copy code and open the official page. The tracking handle is synced and locked while logged in; otherwise it is editable.

sections.title: 06 / Make it yours
sections.body: Settings has Environment checks, Basic settings, Coding settings and AI assistance tabs. Under Coding, choose the default language, starter templates, tools and local limits. Imports no longer ask for a language; automatic downloads have no per-contest switch.

sections.title: 07 / Translate statements
sections.body: Under AI assistance, set Base URL, model and API Key and test the live connection. Enable translation and choose its target language. Every {{language}} in the English default prompt is replaced before sending; restoring defaults requires confirmation. AI translation is optional and off by default. Translation switches and target language now save immediately; prompt edits save automatically after a short pause.

sections.title: 08 / Configure AI caching
sections.body: The shared AI input/output LRU defaults to 100 entries and 50 MB. Either limit evicts least recently used requests. Disabling it preserves entries but skips request cache reads/writes; connection tests always contact the provider.

docs.trouble: If a statement will not download
docs.troubleBody: Retry the problem download later. Site verification may block anonymous requests. Existing solutions, custom cases, and cached statements are preserved. Keep the official website as your fallback.

privacy.title: Privacy & licensing.
privacy.intro: This page describes the current early-preview website and extension. It is not a promise about services that have not launched.

sections.title: This website
sections.body: This site has no Codeforces Workbench account, payment forms, analytics SDK or advertising trackers. The root uses browser language preferences to select a supported URL, with English fallback. Explicit language URLs stay selected. Hosting providers may process access requests and operational logs under their policies.

sections.title: The extension
sections.body: Code, tests and downloaded data stay locally unless you choose an online action. Confirmed one-click submission uploads the current source to Codeforces; copy-and-open writes it to the clipboard. Optional AI translation sends statements and your prompt to your configured provider. API keys use VS Code SecretStorage; the configurable local cache stores AI request input/output, never raw API keys.

sections.title: External services
sections.body: Codeforces login/submission and optional AI requests contact their respective providers directly. Site verification can block Codeforces actions. AI usage may be billed under your provider plan. GitHub, Codeforces, hosting and AI providers apply their own policies; the site and local extension are separate.

sections.title: Licensing
sections.body: The extension has not selected an open-source license; do not assume permission for commercial reuse. The CF Tool development fork retains its upstream MIT license. This website's original code and content are all rights reserved, except for third-party components under their own licenses.

sections.title: Questions
sections.body: For product or privacy questions, open an issue in the extension repository. Do not include passwords, cookies, source code you want to keep private, or other sensitive information in a public issue.
